extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural requirements, and compatibility conditions for Θ-Hodge theaters, D-prime-strips, their morphisms/poly-morphisms, and the combinatorial/´etale/Frobenius 'pictures' used in Inter-Universal Teichmüller Theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-link existence (full poly-isomorphism nonempty)
rubrics_metrics.description: For two Θ-Hodge theaters †HT Θ and ‡HT Θ (relative to the same initial Θ-data), the full poly-isomorphism between the respective collections of data †F(cid:4)_tht mod and ‡F(cid:4)_mod is nonempty; this nonempty full poly-isomorphism is called the Θ-link from †HT Θ to ‡HT Θ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Θ-link is the fundamental relation connecting Θ-Hodge theaters; see Corollary 3.7 (i). Many distinct such isomorphisms may exist and none need be distinguished as 'canonical' (Remark 3.7.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of D under Θ-link
rubrics_metrics.description: For each v ∈ V the tautological isomorphisms (cid:5)D(cid:4)_v for the two theaters (arising from definitions or product functors depending on v ∈ Vgood or Vbad) compose with the Θ-link-induced poly-isomorphism to yield a composite full poly-isomorphism †D(cid:4)_v ∼→ †DΘ_v ∼→ ‡D(cid:4)_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes that the Θ-link respects the 'D' (base-category) data of the theaters (Corollary 3.7 (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of local units O× under Θ-link
rubrics_metrics.description: For each v ∈ V the tautological isomorphisms O×†C(cid:4)_v ∼→ O×†CΘ_v ∼→ O×‡C(cid:4)_v (arising from definitions or natural product functors) compose with the Θ-link-induced poly-isomorphism to give an overall poly-isomorphism of the local unit data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures Θ-links also respect the unit/group-like monoid structures that lie over the D-data (Corollary 3.7 (iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture: infinite oriented chain of Θ-Hodge theaters
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Z-indexed collection {nHT Θ}n∈Z of distinct Θ-Hodge theaters, applying successive Θ-links yields an infinite oriented chain ... → (n−1)HT Θ Θ−→ nHT Θ Θ−→ (n+1)HT Θ → ... which can be viewed as an oriented graph (the 'Frobenius-picture') admitting a natural Z-translation symmetry but not arbitrary permutation symmetries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Frobenius-picture is 'Frobenius-like' or 'order-conscious' (Corollary 3.8 and discussion). In particular it does not admit an automorphism switching two adjacent vertices while fixing others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central role of Θ-link maps in Frobenius-picture
rubrics_metrics.description: A central defining aspect of the Frobenius-picture is that the Θ-link maps send nΘ_v (for v ∈ Vbad) to (n+1)q_v — i.e., the Θ-link maps implement transitions nΘ_v (cid:15)→ (n+1)q_v — reflecting the involvement of the divisor monoid ('q_v') portion of Frobenioids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes that the divisor-monoid/Frobenius part of the Frobenioids induces the Frobenius-like nature of the whole picture (Remark 3.8.1 (i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-picture as canonical splitting with permutation symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an ´etale-picture diagram (Fig. 3.2) relating the sequence of nDv's and the fixed D(cid:4)_v where the horizontal/vertical '— —' denote the extension/relationship; unlike the Frobenius-picture, the ´etale-picture admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among the integer labels n, and may be viewed as a canonical splitting of the Frobenius-picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A related diagram including local units O× (Fig. 3.3) similarly admits permutation symmetry; these canonical splittings underpin later constructions (Corollary 3.9 (i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic core (the (−)D(cid:4)_v invariant)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection (−)D(cid:4)_v constitutes a 'mono-analytic core' (a fixed underlying real-analytic surface associated to a number field) which is essentially fixed as an invariant across the Frobenius-picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulating relative to [AbsTopIII] language, (−)D(cid:4)_v is the mono-analytic core; this is used to think of Frobenius- vs. ´etale-pictures and analogies with Teichmüller theory (Remark 3.9.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a D-prime-strip (holomorphic base-prime-strip)
rubrics_metrics.description: A D-prime-strip †D = {†Dv}v∈V (relative to given initial Θ-data) must satisfy: (a) if v ∈ Vnon then †Dv is a category admitting an equivalence †Dv ∼→ Dv (Dv as in Examples 3.2, 3.3); (b) if v ∈ Varc then †Dv is an Aut-holomorphic orbispace isomorphic to Dv (as in Example 3.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furthermore π1(†Dv) functorially determines a topological/profinite group corresponding to 'C_v' and one obtains natural morphisms †Dv → †D_v; these constructions allow defining cusps and label-classes from †Dv alone (Definition 4.1 (i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Label classes of cusps and canonical F_l-torsor structure
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ V, LabCusp(†Dv) is the set of label classes of cusps of †Dv lying over a single 'nonzero cusp'; LabCusp(†Dv) admits a natural F(cid:2)_l-torsor structure and from †Dv one canonically constructs a distinguished element †η_v ∈ LabCusp(†Dv) determined by (cid:2)v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This torsor structure and canonical element are fundamental for later identifications and for the F_l-actions used in constructing capsules and poly-actions (Definition 4.1 (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a D(cid:4)-prime-strip (mono-analytic prime-strip)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mono-analytic base-prime-strip †D(cid:4) = {†D(cid:4)_v}v∈V must satisfy: (a) if v ∈ Vnon then †D(cid:4)_v admits an equivalence ∼→ D(cid:4)_v (as in Examples 3.2); (b) if v ∈ Varc then †D(cid:4)_v is an object of TM(cid:4) and is isomorphic to D(cid:4)_v (Definition 4.1 (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To any D-prime-strip †D one can associate a mono-analyticization †D(cid:4) by appropriate subcategory choices at nonarchimedean primes or constructions at archimedean primes (Definition 4.1 (iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms and capsules of D- and D(cid:4)-prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of D- (resp. D(cid:4)-) prime-strips is a collection of morphisms indexed by V between constituent objects. Capsules are collections of prime-strips; morphisms of capsules are defined componentwise (Definition 4.1 (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notions provide the category-level framework for defining poly-morphisms and capsule-level actions used later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of poly-morphism to D(cid:6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given †D(cid:6) equivalent to D(cid:6) and a D-prime-strip †D = {†Dv}, a poly-morphism †Dv → †D(cid:6) is a collection of morphisms †Dv → †D(cid:6) (using §0 conventions for v ∈ Vnon and the construction in (v) for v ∈ Varc). A poly-morphism †D → †D(cid:6) is the collection of such maps for all v; capsules map similarly (Definition 4.1 (vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poly-morphisms formalize simultaneous local-to-global maps from the family of local prime-strip data into the global D(cid:6) context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical bijections of LabCusp across places (Proposition 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a D-prime-strip †D = {†Dv}v∈V and any v,w ∈ V there exist bijections LabCusp(†Dv) ∼→ LabCusp(†Dw) uniquely determined by compatibility with the canonical elements †η_v and the F_l-torsor structures. Identifying these gives LabCusp(†D) with a canonical element and an F_l-torsor; in particular LabCusp(†D) ≅ F_l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bijections are preserved by arbitrary isomorphisms of D-prime-strips (Proposition 4.2). Remark 4.2.1 warns that alternate choices of 'Dv' could break these bijections in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model base-NF-bridge automorphism subgroup identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The subgroup Aut(cid:4)(C_K) ⊆ Aut(C_K) (elements fixing the cusp (cid:2)) maps, via the action on l-torsion of Δ_ab_X ⊗ F_l, into GL2(F_l)/{±1}; the images are identified with 'semi-unipotent, up to ±1' and 'Borel' subgroups. Define AutSL(cid:4)(C_K) and AutSL(C_K) as subgroups acting trivially on F(μ_l). Associated subsets V±un = Aut(cid:4)(C_K)·V and VBor = Aut(C_K)·V inside V(K) arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a group-theoretic algorithm reconstructing Aut(cid:4)(D(cid:6)) ⊆ Aut(D(cid:6)) from π1(D(cid:6)), so these subgroup/subset structures are recoverable from the profinite fundamental group (Example 4.3 (i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of NF poly-morphisms φNF_v and their form
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Vnon (resp. Varc) there is a natural poly-morphism φNF_v: Dv → D(cid:6) given by the collection of morphisms of the form β ◦ φNF_•,v ◦ α where α ∈ Aut(Dv) (identified with Aut(X−→v) or Aut(X_v)) and β ∈ Aut(cid:4)(D(cid:6)) (Example 4.3 (ii),(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These poly-morphisms encode the 'tautological' local-to-global embeddings and are equivariant/stabilized by the action of Aut(cid:4)(C_K) (Example 4.3 (iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capsule D(cid:2) and F_l-equivariance of φNF_j
rubrics_metrics.description: For each j ∈ F_l define a copy Dj of the tautological D-prime-strip and a poly-morphism φNF_j: Dj → D(cid:6); the capsule D(cid:2) = {Dj}_j∈F_l and the poly-morphism φNF_(cid:2): D(cid:2) → D(cid:6) are equivariant with respect to the natural F_l poly-action on D(cid:6) and the permutation poly-action on the capsule (Example 4.3 (iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields a natural poly-action of F_l on the triple (D(cid:2), D(cid:6), φNF_(cid:2)) used in later arithmetic-local-analytic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three required properties for the 'desired geometry'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'desired geometry' to work with arithmetic local-analytic sections (prime-strips) must satisfy: (a) local independence of global structures, (b) globalizability in a fashion independent of local structures, and (c) be based on ´etale-like structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These apparently competing requirements motivate the use of absolute p-adic mono-anabelian geometry and panalocalization in later chapters (Remark 4.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obstructions / incompatibilities of prime-strip sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'arithmetic local-analytic sections' given by D-prime-strips fail to be arithmetically holomorphic because (a) they do not extend to ring homomorphisms K → F, (b) they do not extend compatibly to prime decomposition trees (isomorphism between v and v(cid:8) does not extend to full decomposition trees), and (c) local absolute Galois isomorphisms fail to extend to a global section GF → GK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These points (a)-(c) explain why global arithmetic structures are incompatible with the naive local-analytic sections and why further anabelian/mono-analytic technology is necessary (Remark 4.3.1 (i)-(iii)).
